name: How do I design an ADU that will rent well later?

mainEntity.name: How do I design an ADU that will rent well later in Los Angeles without overbuilding it?
mainEntity.text: How do I design an ADU that will rent well later in Los Angeles without overbuilding it?

acceptedAnswer.text: A good rental ADU balances appeal and practicality. Renters usually value privacy, natural light, a comfortable living area, in-unit laundry if possible, storage, and a clean modern finish. The design should feel independent from the main home, with its own entry and a clear separation between indoor and outdoor spaces. At the same time, the project should avoid costly features that do not improve marketability, such as oversized rooms, elaborate roof forms, or high-maintenance specialty materials. Efficient layouts usually rent better than flashy ones because they are easier to furnish and maintain. Homeowners should also think about noise control, utility access, and long-term repair costs. A well-designed rental ADU should attract tenants while still being simple to build and operate. That balance is usually more valuable than maximizing every possible square foot.
acceptedAnswer.description: A rentable ADU usually has a separate entry, good privacy, practical storage, natural light, efficient kitchen and bath layouts, and durable finishes. It should feel independent, be easy to maintain, and avoid overly expensive features that do not improve tenant demand.
